questions.q: The IOC (investigation of choice) for thyroid cancers is:
questions.exp: IOC: FNAC. (Book p90)

questions.q: Medullary thyroid cancer is associated with which syndrome and gene?
questions.exp: Medullary: MEN2 syndrome; Gene: RET. (Book p90)

questions.q: Cowden syndrome (↑ risk of breast & thyroid cancer, benign GI polyps) is associated with which histology and gene?
questions.exp: Follicular: Cowden syndrome (↑ breast & thyroid cancer risk, GI polyps benign) - PTEN gene: Ch 10. (Book p90)

questions.q: Werner/adult progeroid syndrome (follicular cancer association) involves which gene?
questions.exp: Werner/Adult progeroid syndrome: WRN gene. (Book p90)

questions.q: Familial adenomatous polyposis (≥100 polyps, 100% colorectal cancer risk) is associated with which thyroid histology?
questions.exp: Papillary associations: FAP (≥100 polyps, 100% colorectal cancer risk), Cowden, Carney complex, familial non-medullary & familial papillary syndromes. (Book p90)

questions.q: Carney complex is also known as:
questions.exp: Carney complex/Batman's syndrome - papillary association. (Book p90)

questions.q: The AP gene (FAP) is on which chromosome, and PRKAR1A links to which histology?
questions.exp: Papillary genes: AP gene Ch 5, PTEN, PRKAR1A. (Book p90)

questions.q: T1 thyroid tumor size is:
questions.exp: T1: Tumor ≤ 2cm (T1a ≤ 1cm; T1b > 1cm but ≤ 2cm). (Book p90)

questions.q: T1b thyroid tumor is:
questions.exp: T1b: Tumor > 1cm but ≤ 2cm. (Book p90)

questions.q: T2 thyroid tumor is:
questions.exp: T2: Tumor > 2cm but ≤ 4cm. (Book p90)

questions.q: T3a thyroid tumor is:
opts: Tumor > 4 cm with strap muscle invasion
questions.exp: T3a: Tumor > 4cm limited to thyroid. (Book p90)

questions.q: T3b (recent update) is a tumor of:
opts: Any size invading only strap muscles
Any size with major neck structure invasion
questions.exp: T3b: Tumor of any size invading ONLY strap muscles (recent update). (Book p90)

questions.q: T4 thyroid tumor denotes:
opts: Gross extrathyroidal extension into major neck structures
questions.exp: T4: Gross extrathyroidal extension into major neck structures. (Book p90)

questions.q: N1 in thyroid cancer means:
questions.exp: N1: Metastasis to regional nodes (N0 none; Nx can't be assessed). (Book p90)

questions.q: M1 in thyroid cancer means:
questions.exp: M0: No distant metastasis; M1: Distant metastasis (+). (Book p90)

questions.q: Differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) includes:
questions.exp: DTC: Papillary, follicular, Hurthle cell - arise from thyroid epithelial cells & take up iodine. (Book p91)

questions.q: DTC diagnosed at <55 years carries:
questions.exp: Updates: DTC Dx by age - <55 yrs good prognosis; >55 yrs bad prognosis. (Book p91)

questions.q: Which cancer (previously staged T4) is now staged the same as DTC?
questions.exp: Anaplastic cancer (previously T4): staged same as DTC. (Book p91)

questions.q: The most common thyroid cancer is:
questions.exp: PTC: m/c thyroid cancer with BEST prognosis. (Book p91)

questions.q: Which is NOT a listed risk factor for PTC?
questions.exp: Risk factors: 1. Radiation exposure; 2. Family history; 3. Obesity (iodine deficiency is FTC's). (Book p91)

questions.q: Radiation exposure risk includes all EXCEPT:
opts: Radioiodine ablation therapy at old age
Radioiodine ablation therapy at young age
questions.exp: Radiation: nuclear fall out, post radiotherapy head & neck, radioiodine ablation at YOUNG age. (Book p91)

questions.q: PTC genes exposed to radiation are:
questions.exp: PTC genes exposed to radiation are more aggressive. (Book p91)

questions.q: The most common (m/c) mutation in PTC is:
questions.exp: Genetics: mutation of BRAF (m/c), GDNF, RET/PTC. (Book p91)

questions.q: GDNF stands for:
questions.exp: GDNF: Glial derived neurotrophic factor. (Book p91)

questions.q: The female:male ratio and decade for PTC are:
questions.exp: Incidence: Female:male = 3:1; 3rd-5th decade. (Book p91)

questions.q: The most common presentation of PTC is:
questions.exp: Thyroid swelling: m/c presentation; B/L multicentric → Rx: total thyroidectomy. (Book p91)

questions.q: The FIRST lymphatic spread of PTC is to:
questions.exp: Lymphatic: Level 6 lymph nodes 1st (central compartment/delphian lymph nodes). (Book p92)

questions.q: The most common site of haematogenous spread in PTC is:
questions.exp: Haematogenous: Lungs (m/c). (Book p92)

questions.q: Lateral aberrant thyroid is:
opts: Level 6 LN enlargement (d/t PTC) with non-palpable thyroid
questions.exp: Lateral aberrant thyroid: level 6 LN enlargement (d/t PTC) & non-palpable thyroid. (Book p92)

questions.q: A thyroid incidentaloma is:
questions.exp: Thyroid incidentaloma: incidental Dx; size < 1cm. (Book p92)

questions.q: The IOC for diagnosing PTC is:
questions.exp: Ix: FNAC = IOC. (Book p92)

questions.q: 'Orphan Annie eyed'/coffee bean nuclei on H&E indicate:
questions.exp: Orphan Annie eyed/coffee bean nuclei - PTC. (Book p92)

questions.q: Pseudo (intranuclear) inclusions are a feature of:
questions.exp: Pseudo (intranuclear) inclusions - PTC. (Book p92)

questions.q: Psammoma bodies are:
questions.exp: Psammoma bodies: foci of dystrophic calcification. (Book p92)

questions.q: Psammoma bodies are seen in all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Psammoma bodies: PTC, serous cystadenoma of ovary, papillary RCC, meningioma. (Book p92)

questions.q: Hemithyroidectomy criteria include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Hemithyroidectomy: ALL of - low risk, U/L, 1-4 cm, NO extrathyroidal spread. (Book p93)

questions.q: Minimum total thyroidectomy is indicated for all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Minimum total thyroidectomy: radiation induced DTC, familial non-medullary TC, multifocal B/L DTC, extrathyroid extension. (Book p93)

questions.q: Prophylactic central neck dissection (total thyroidectomy + CND) is done for:
questions.exp: Total thyroidectomy + CND (level 6 LN removal): T3, T4 (prophylactic CND done); level 6 LN (+). (Book p93)

questions.q: Total thyroidectomy + CND + modified radical neck dissection (U/L or B/L) is for:
opts: PTC involving level 6 + other neck LN
questions.exp: Total + CND + MRND (U/L/B/L): PTC involving level 6 + other neck LN. (Book p93)

questions.q: The prerequisite TSH level for a whole body iodine scan is:
questions.exp: Prerequisite: TSH > 30 to enhance iodine uptake. (Book p93)

questions.q: In the traditional method of raising TSH, thyroxine is not supplemented for 4-6 weeks; the disadvantage is:
questions.exp: Traditional: wait 4-6 weeks post Sx, don't supplement thyroxine - patient suffers hypothyroidism 4-6 weeks. (Book p93)

questions.q: The alternative to thyroxine withdrawal for raising TSH is:
questions.exp: Recombinant TSH injections avoid withdrawal hypothyroidism. (Book p93)

questions.q: A positive whole body iodine scan (residual disease/mets) is treated with:
questions.exp: (+) scan → Rx: Radioiodine ablation (RIA). (Book p94)

questions.q: RIA uses I-131 which acts via:
questions.exp: I131 acts via β rays. (Book p94)

questions.q: The half life of I-131 is:
questions.exp: I131 ½ life: 7-8 days. (Book p94)

questions.q: Indications for RIA include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: RIA indications: residual disease, metastases, +ve lymph nodes, persistently high thyroglobulin after Sx. (Book p94)

questions.q: A negative scan is managed with TSH suppression to the lower limit of normal using:
questions.exp: (-) scan → TSH suppression to lower limit of N: thyroxine (↓ recurrence of PTC). (Book p94)

questions.q: Life-long follow-up of DTC uses USG neck plus which tumor marker, checked 6-monthly?
questions.exp: Life-long follow-up: USG neck + S. thyroglobulin (tumor marker for DTC) 6-monthly. (Book p94)

questions.q: S. thyroglobulin is NOT a reliable marker if:
questions.exp: Not reliable if anti-Tg antibodies (+). (Book p94)

questions.q: Immunotherapy (targeted therapy) for radioiodine-resistant DTC includes:
questions.exp: RAI-resistant DTC: 1. Immunotherapy sorafenib, lenvatinib; 2. EBRT; 3. Chemo doxorubicin. (Book p94)

questions.q: The chemotherapy drug for radioiodine-resistant DTC is:
questions.exp: Chemotherapy: doxorubicin. (Book p94)

questions.q: Lindsey tumor is:
opts: Follicular variety of papillary with similar prognosis as PTC
A variant of FTC with poor prognosis
questions.exp: Lindsey tumor: follicular variety of papillary; similar prognosis as PTC. (Book p94)

questions.q: The second most common thyroid cancer is:
questions.exp: FTC: 2nd m/c thyroid cancer; m/c cancer in iodine deficient areas. (Book p94)

questions.q: FTC genetics shows upregulation of miRNA:
questions.exp: Genetics: upregulation of miRNA-197, 346; mutation of PTEN & BAX gene. (Book p94)

questions.q: The genes mutated in FTC are:
questions.exp: Mutation of PTEN & BAX gene. (Book p94)

questions.q: The risk factor for FTC is:
questions.exp: Risk factor: long standing multinodular goitre; Females > males. (Book p95)

questions.q: Pressure symptoms in FTC: trachea causes stridor and RLN causes:
questions.exp: Pressure: trachea → stridor; RLN → hoarseness. (Book p95)

questions.q: Haematogenous spread of FTC classically produces:
opts: Pulsatile bony mets (highly vascular, osteolytic > osteoblastic)
questions.exp: Haematogenous: pulsatile bony mets - highly vascular; osteolytic > osteoblastic. (Book p95)

questions.sec: FTC: Dx, Mx & Hurthle Cell Carcinoma
questions.q: FNAC in FTC reports:
questions.exp: FNAC: follicular neoplasm (Thy 3). (Book p95)

questions.sec: FTC: Dx, Mx & Hurthle Cell Carcinoma
questions.q: FNAC cannot differentiate:
questions.exp: Cannot differentiate follicular adenoma vs carcinoma on FNAC. (Book p95)

questions.sec: FTC: Dx, Mx & Hurthle Cell Carcinoma
questions.q: The adenoma vs carcinoma distinction is made by:
questions.exp: Hemithyroidectomy → frozen section: cancer → mx same as PTC; adenoma → no mx. (Book p95)

questions.sec: FTC: Dx, Mx & Hurthle Cell Carcinoma
questions.q: FTC prognosis compared to PTC is:
questions.exp: Prognosis: slightly poorer than PTC. (Book p95)

questions.sec: FTC: Dx, Mx & Hurthle Cell Carcinoma
questions.q: Hurthle cell carcinoma presents in which decade and the cells are rich in:
questions.exp: Hurthle cell carcinoma: 6th-7th decade; oxyphilic Hurthle cells rich in mitochondria. (Book p95)

questions.sec: FTC: Dx, Mx & Hurthle Cell Carcinoma
questions.q: Compared to other DTC, Hurthle cell carcinoma is:
questions.exp: More aggressive than FTC; LESS radioactive avid than other DTC; mx same as PTC; prognosis poorer than FTC. (Book p95)

questions.sec: FTC: Dx, Mx & Hurthle Cell Carcinoma
questions.q: Hurthle cells are seen in all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Hurthle cells seen in: Hurthle cell carcinoma, Hashimoto thyroiditis, thyroid lymphoma. (Book p96)

questions.q: The AGES system comprises:
opts: Age, histologic grade, extrathyroidal invasion, size
Metastases, age, completeness of resection, invasion, size
questions.exp: AGES: Age, histologic Grade, Extrathyroidal invasion, Size. (Book p96)

questions.q: The AMES system comprises:
opts: Age, metastases, extrathyroidal spread, size of tumors
questions.exp: AMES: Age, Metastases, Extrathyroidal spread, Size of tumors. (Book p96)

questions.q: The 'C' (completeness of original surgical resection - post op criteria) belongs to:
questions.exp: MACIS: Metastases, Age, Completeness of original surgical resection (post op criteria), extrathyroidal invasion, size of original lesion. (Book p96)

questions.q: The least common thyroid cancer with the worst prognosis is:
questions.exp: Anaplastic: least common type; WORST prognosis. (Book p96)

questions.q: Anaplastic carcinoma incidence peaks in:
questions.exp: Incidence: 5th-7th decade. (Book p96)

questions.q: Anaplastic genetics shows:
opts: miRNA 17-92 upregulation; mutation in p53 & B-catenin
questions.exp: Genetics: miRNA 17-92 upregulation; mutation in p53 & B-catenin. (Book p96)

questions.q: Anaplastic neck swelling is characteristically:
opts: Rapid ↑ in size, hard in consistency
questions.exp: Neck swelling: rapid ↑ in size, hard in consistency; H/o multinodular goitre (follicular > anaplastic). (Book p96)

questions.q: The important differential diagnosis of anaplastic carcinoma is:
questions.exp: D/D: Riedel thyroiditis (fibrosis of thyroid gland). (Book p96)

questions.q: Spread of anaplastic carcinoma is predominantly:
questions.exp: Spread: distant metastases - lungs (m/c). (Book p96)

questions.q: FNAC in anaplastic carcinoma is often inconclusive; next step is:
questions.exp: FNAC inconclusive → USG guided core biopsy. (Book p96)

questions.q: Staging of anaplastic carcinoma is:
questions.exp: Staging is same as DTC. (Book p97)

questions.q: Localised anaplastic disease is managed aggressively with:
opts: Total thyroidectomy + CND + modified radical neck dissection
questions.exp: Localised: aggressive mx - Sx total thyroidectomy + CND + MRND. (Book p97)

questions.q: In advanced anaplastic disease, isthmusectomy is done to:
questions.exp: Advanced/metastatic: tumor debulking; isthmusectomy (↓ pressure over trachea); TKI dabrafenib (immunotherapy); chemotherapy. (Book p97)

questions.q: The tyrosine kinase inhibitor named for advanced anaplastic cancer is:
questions.exp: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors: dabrafenib (immunotherapy). (Book p97)

questions.q: The most common type of thyroid lymphoma is:
questions.exp: Types: DLBCL (m/c); small blue cell. (Book p97)

questions.q: The risk factor for thyroid lymphoma is:
questions.exp: Risk factor: long standing Hashimoto/lymphocytic thyroiditis; 5th-7th decade; rare. (Book p97)

questions.q: B symptoms of lymphoma include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: B symptoms: weight loss, fever, night sweats, itching; thyroid swelling m/c. (Book p97)

questions.q: The investigation of choice for thyroid lymphoma is:
questions.exp: Core/trucut biopsy (FNAC cannot characterize a lymphoma). (Book p97)

questions.q: The 1st line Rx of thyroid lymphoma is:
questions.exp: Chemotherapy 1st line Rx: R-CHOP. (Book p97)

questions.q: In R-CHOP, 'R' is rituximab which is a monoclonal antibody against:
questions.exp: R: rituximab (monoclonal antibody against CD20). (Book p97)

questions.q: In R-CHOP, 'H' and 'O' stand for:
questions.exp: H: hydroxydaunorubicin; O: oncovin/vincristine; C cyclophosphamide; P prednisolone. (Book p97)

questions.q: Surgery in thyroid lymphoma is indicated:
questions.exp: Sx indication: only in residual/recurrent disease. (Book p97)

questions.q: Medullary thyroid carcinoma arises from:
questions.exp: Arises from parafollicular/C cells (neural crest → ultimobranchial bodies → C cells). (Book p98)

questions.q: MTC secretes all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Secrete: calcitonin, CEA, chromogranin A. (Book p98)

questions.q: In MTC, a sign of dedifferentiation (more aggressive) is:
questions.exp: CEA: sign of dedifferentiation (more aggressive). (Book p98)

questions.q: Chromogranin A is also released in:
questions.exp: Chromogranin A also released in carcinoid tumors. (Book p98)

questions.q: The more common (m/c) type of MTC is:
questions.exp: Sporadic: m/c, 4th-6th decade, less aggressive; familial: MEN2 syndromes, more aggressive, multifocal. (Book p98)

questions.q: The most aggressive MTC is associated with:
questions.exp: MEN 2B: most aggressive. (Book p98)

questions.q: Diarrhoea in MTC is due to:
questions.exp: Diarrhoea: serotonin. (Book p98)

questions.q: Cushing syndrome in MTC is due to:
questions.exp: Cushing syndrome: ACTH. (Book p98)

questions.q: Flushing in MTC is due to:
questions.exp: Flushing: histamine. (Book p98)

questions.q: H&E of MTC classically shows:
questions.exp: Amyloid rich stroma. (Book p98)

questions.q: Haematogenous spread of MTC is most commonly to:
questions.exp: Lymphatic: level 6 LNs; haematogenous: liver (m/c). (Book p98)

questions.q: The 1st line Mx of MTC is:
questions.exp: Sx: 1st line Mx. (Book p99)

questions.q: Tumor localized to thyroid in MTC is treated with:
questions.exp: Localized to thyroid: total thyroidectomy + CND. (Book p99)

questions.q: Tumor involving thyroid + level 6 + other LN in MTC needs:
opts: Total thyroidectomy + CND + MRND on B/L sides
questions.exp: Thyroid + level 6 & other LN: total + CND + MRND on B/L sides. (Book p99)

questions.q: Whole body iodine scan/RIA in MTC has:
opts: No role (cells do not take up iodine)
questions.exp: No role in MTC - cells do not take up iodine. (Book p99)

questions.q: Before treating MTC, always rule out which MEN2 association that must be managed FIRST?
questions.exp: Rule out pheochromocytoma (managed FIRST, then MTC); hyperparathyroidism managed together. (Book p99)

questions.q: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors for advanced MTC are:
questions.exp: Advanced: tumor debulking, radiotherapy, TKI vandetinib, carbozantinib. (Book p99)

questions.q: Follow-up markers of MTC are:
questions.exp: Follow up: calcitonin & CEA. (Book p99)

questions.q: Match the genetics: follicular thyroid carcinoma shows:
questions.exp: Follicular: K-RAS, PI3K (papillary BRAF/RET-PTC; medullary RET/MEN II; anaplastic P53). (Book p99)

questions.q: The metastasis pattern of medullary and anaplastic cancers is:
questions.exp: Papillary lymphatic; follicular haematogenous (bony mets); medullary & anaplastic BOTH. (Book p99)

questions.q: The origin of anaplastic carcinoma is:
questions.exp: Anaplastic origin: follicular cells (medullary: parafollicular cells). (Book p99)

questions.q: Risk factors for papillary cancer include radiation, thyroglossal cyst and:
questions.exp: Papillary risk: radiation, thyroglossal cyst, Hashimoto's thyroiditis; follicular: iodine deficiency, MNG. (Book p99)

questions.q: On H&E, medullary carcinoma shows:
questions.exp: H&E: papillary - Orphan Annie eye, psammoma; follicular - follicles; medullary - amyloid. (Book p99)

questions.q: MEN 1 (Wermer syndrome) is due to mutation of:
questions.exp: MEN1 (Wermer): menin gene on Ch 11. (Book p100)

questions.q: The most common pituitary adenoma in MEN1 is:
questions.exp: 3 Ps: pituitary adenomas (prolactinoma m/c). (Book p100)

questions.q: The most common abnormality in MEN1 (95% cases) is:
questions.exp: Parathyroid abnormalities (m/c: 95% cases): adenoma >> hyperplasia. (Book p100)

questions.q: The most common pancreatic endocrine tumor overall vs in MEN1 are respectively:
questions.exp: Pancreatic: m/c overall insulinoma; in MEN1 gastrinoma; non-functional PPoma. (Book p100)

questions.q: The non-functional pancreatic tumor seen in MEN1 is:
questions.exp: Non functional pancreatic tumor: PPoma. (Book p100)

questions.q: Other tumors seen in MEN1 include:
questions.exp: Also collagenomas, adrenocortical tumors, thymic tumors. (Book p100)

questions.q: MEN 2 syndrome is due to:
questions.exp: RET proto-oncogene on Ch 10. (Book p100)

questions.q: The MEN2 type with MTC only carries exon mutation:
questions.exp: Types: MTC only (exon 618), MEN 2A, MEN 2B. (Book p100)

questions.q: MEN 2A (Sipple syndrome) features include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: 2A: MTC m/c, parathyroid (adenoma > hyperplasia), pheochromocytoma, megacolon/Hirschsprung (2A > 2B); exon 634. (Book p100)

questions.q: The '5 Ms' (MTC m/c most aggressive, marfanoid, mucosal neuromas, medullated corneal fibres, megacolon) describe:
questions.exp: MEN 2B (MEN3): 5 Ms; exon 918; medullated corneal fibres cause visual problems. (Book p100)

questions.q: Megacolon/Hirschsprung disease is more common in:
questions.exp: Megacolon/Hirschsprung disease: MEN 2A > 2B. (Book p100)

questions.q: Who should undergo RET testing?
questions.exp: 1st degree relatives should undergo RET testing. (Book p101)

questions.q: Low risk RET mutations (exons 768, 790) need prophylactic thyroidectomy:
questions.exp: Low: 768, 790 → upto 20 years. (Book p101)

questions.q: Medium risk RET mutations (exons 618, 634) need prophylactic thyroidectomy:
questions.exp: Medium: 618, 634 → upto 5-6 years. (Book p101)

questions.q: High risk RET mutation (exon 918) needs prophylactic thyroidectomy:
questions.exp: High: 918 → before 1 year. (Book p101)

questions.q: If tumor is +ve, the pentagastrin stimulation test shows:
questions.exp: If tumor +ve → pentagastrin stimulation test → ↑↑ calcitonin. (Book p101)

questions.q: MEN 4 syndrome is due to:
questions.exp: MEN4: CDKN1B gene on Ch 12. (Book p101)

questions.q: Features of MEN4 include pituitary, parathyroid adenomas plus:
questions.exp: MEN4: pituitary adenomas, parathyroid adenomas, renal tumors, adrenocortical tumors, reproductive organ tumors. (Book p101)

units.title: Thyroid Cancers: IOC & Syndromes
units.guide: IOC for thyroid cancers is FNAC. Syndrome links: medullary → MEN2/RET; follicular → Cowden (PTEN Ch10, ↑ breast & thyroid cancer, benign GI polyps) & Werner (WRN); papillary → FAP (AP Ch5, ≥100 polyps, 100% colorectal risk), Cowden, Carney/Batman's, PRKAR1A.

units.title: TNM Staging
units.guide: T1 ≤2cm (1a ≤1cm, 1b >1-≤2cm); T2 >2-≤4cm; T3a >4cm limited to thyroid; T3b any size invading ONLY strap muscles (recent update); T4 gross extension into major neck structures. N1 regional nodes; M1 distant mets.

units.title: DTC & Updates
units.guide: DTC = papillary + follicular + Hurthle cell: arise from epithelial cells and take up iodine. New rule: age cutoff 55 - younger good prognosis, older bad; anaplastic (previously T4) now staged like DTC.

units.title: PTC: Risk Factors & Genetics
units.guide: PTC = m/c thyroid cancer with best prognosis. Risks: radiation (fallout, head-neck RT, RAI at young age - more aggressive tumors), family history, obesity. Genetics BRAF (m/c), GDNF, RET/PTC. F:M 3:1, 3rd-5th decade.

units.title: PTC: Clinical Features & Spread
units.guide: Presents as thyroid swelling, B/L multicentric → total thyroidectomy. Lymphatic first to level 6 (central/delphian), haematogenous to lungs. Lateral aberrant thyroid = level 6 LN mets with non-palpable gland; incidentaloma <1cm.

units.title: PTC: Diagnosis & Histology
units.guide: FNAC is IOC. Histology: Orphan Annie eyed/coffee bean nuclei, pseudo intranuclear inclusions, psammoma bodies (dystrophic calcification - also in serous cystadenoma ovary, papillary RCC, meningioma).

units.title: PTC: Surgical Options
units.guide: Hemithyroidectomy when ALL: low risk, U/L, 1-4 cm, no extrathyroidal spread. Minimum total for radiation-induced, familial non-medullary, multifocal B/L, extrathyroid extension. Add CND for T3/T4 or level 6 (+); add MRND when level 6 + other neck nodes.

units.title: Whole Body Iodine Scan & RIA
units.sec: Whole Body Iodine Scan & RIA · p93
units.guide: Post-Sx scan needs TSH >30 (withdraw thyroxine 4-6 wks - patient hypothyroid - or recombinant TSH). (+) scan → RIA with I131 (β rays, t½ 7-8 d) for residual/mets/+ve nodes/high Tg; (-) → thyroxine TSH suppression + life-long 6-monthly USG & thyroglobulin (unreliable if anti-Tg Ab +).

units.title: Radioiodine Resistant DTC & Lindsey Tumor
units.sec: Radioiodine Resistant DTC & Lindsey Tumor · p94
units.guide: RAI-resistant DTC: sorafenib/lenvatinib, EBRT, doxorubicin. Lindsey tumor = follicular variety of papillary, prognosis like PTC.

units.title: FTC: Basics, Features & Spread
units.guide: 2nd m/c; m/c in iodine deficiency; risk long-standing MNG; females > males. miRNA 197/346, PTEN & BAX. Rapid neck swelling, pressure symptoms; pulsatile vascular osteolytic bony mets; lymphatic to level 6.

units.title: FTC: Dx, Mx & Hurthle Cell Carcinoma
units.sec: FTC: Dx, Mx & Hurthle Cell Carcinoma · p95
units.guide: FNAC gives follicular neoplasm (Thy 3) but can't split adenoma vs carcinoma - hemithyroidectomy + frozen section decides. Prognosis slightly poorer than PTC. Hurthle cell: 6th-7th decade, mitochondria-rich oxyphilic cells, less RAI-avid, more aggressive, poorer than FTC; Hurthle cells also in Hashimoto's & thyroid lymphoma.

units.title: Prognostic Scores (AGES/AMES/MACIS)
units.guide: Well-differentiated TC scores: AGES = age, grade, extrathyroidal invasion, size; AMES = age, metastases, extrathyroidal spread, size; MACIS = metastases, age, completeness of original resection (post-op criteria), invasion, size.

units.title: Anaplastic Carcinoma
units.guide: Least common, worst prognosis; 5th-7th decade; miRNA 17-92, p53 & B-catenin. Rapid hard neck swelling on MNG background, pressure symptoms; D/D Riedel thyroiditis; spreads to lungs; FNAC inconclusive → core biopsy. Localised: total + CND + MRND; advanced: debulking, isthmusectomy for tracheal pressure, dabrafenib, chemo.

units.title: Thyroid Lymphoma
units.guide: Rare, 5th-7th decade, on long-standing Hashimoto's. DLBCL m/c; thyroid swelling + B symptoms (weight loss, fever, night sweats, itching). Core/trucut biopsy (FNAC can't characterize). Chemo R-CHOP 1st line (rituximab anti-CD20, cyclophosphamide, hydroxydaunorubicin, oncovin/vincristine, prednisolone); surgery only for residual/recurrent.

units.title: MTC: Origin, Secretions & Types
units.guide: From parafollicular/C cells (neural crest → ultimobranchial bodies). Secretes calcitonin, CEA (dedifferentiation marker), chromogranin A. Sporadic m/c (4th-6th decade); familial = MEN2 (2B most aggressive, multifocal). Atypical symptoms: diarrhoea (serotonin), Cushing (ACTH), flushing (histamine).

units.title: MTC: Dx, Spread & Mx
units.guide: FNAC + amyloid-rich stroma; lymphatic level 6, haematogenous liver. Sx 1st line: total + CND (add MRND as nodal spread widens). No RIA role. Rule out pheochromocytoma FIRST & treat hyperparathyroidism together. Advanced: debulking, RT, vandetinib/carbozantinib; follow-up calcitonin + CEA.

units.title: Summary of Thyroid Cancers
units.guide: Papillary: m/c, best, BRAF/RET-PTC, lymphatic, Orphan Annie + psammoma. Follicular: iodine deficiency/MNG, K-RAS/PI3K, bony mets, follicles. Medullary: parafollicular, RET/MEN2, both routes, amyloid. Anaplastic: L/C, worst, P53, both routes.

units.title: MEN 1 Syndrome
units.guide: Wermer syndrome, menin on Ch 11. 3 Ps: pituitary (prolactinoma m/c), parathyroid (95%, adenoma >> hyperplasia), pancreatic (overall insulinoma, in MEN1 gastrinoma, non-functional PPoma); plus collagenomas, adrenocortical & thymic tumors.

units.title: MEN 2 Syndrome
units.guide: RET on Ch 10. MTC-only exon 618; 2A (Sipple) exon 634: MTC, parathyroid, pheochromocytoma, megacolon/Hirschsprung (2A > 2B); 2B (MEN3) exon 918: 5 Ms - MTC most aggressive, marfanoid, mucosal neuromas, medullated corneal fibres, megacolon.

units.title: RET Testing & MEN 4
units.guide: 1st-degree relatives get RET testing: low (768/790) prophylactic thyroidectomy upto 20 yrs; medium (618/634) upto 5-6 yrs; high (918) before 1 yr. Tumor +ve → pentagastrin stimulation → ↑↑ calcitonin. MEN4 = CDKN1B on Ch 12: pituitary, parathyroid, renal, adrenocortical, reproductive organ tumors.
